A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Model Equality Testing research. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D are readable and matchable, including relocated results and retained qualitative samples.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulation results, finetuning and model-swap experiments, and an audit of 31 commercial endpoints in Sections 4–5, with additional empirical evidence in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds kernel comparisons, temperature-mismatch tests, prompt-distribution analyses, and further numerical results in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The proposed Hamming-MMD procedure, null simulation and permutation algorithms, and composite-null rejection rule remain unchanged. Levenshtein MMD is introduced as an experimental comparator.

E1.justification: Wikipedia in the same five languages, HumanEval, and UltraChat remain the underlying datasets. Appendix C adds an explicit decoding-temperature mismatch scenario and evaluations using language-specific and mixed-task prompt distributions.

E2.justification: v2 adds Levenshtein MMD as a comparator for detecting quantization and watermarking, evaluated on Llama-3 8B, Llama-3 70B, and Mistral 7B in Table 9. The previously evaluated kernels and classical statistical tests are retained.

E3.justification: Added experiments introduce further model/quantization configurations, N=50m character-space testing, temperature contrasts of 1 versus 0.5/1.5, and 50-token task comparisons. Section 4.3 also revises the stated Unicode vocabulary size from approximately 1.1 million to 155063; this does not establish that existing experiments were rerun. The original audit protocol remains unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix C substantially expands sensitivity analysis: it tests whether task openness, language concentration, and task mixing affect power; compares an edit-distance kernel; and examines whether larger samples compensate for reduced character-space power. Additional model-distortion and temperature tests broaden robustness evidence. Existing length, prompt-count, permutation, and asymmetric-sampling analyses remain.

E5.justification: Previously point-only power results gain standard errors in Figure 3 and v1 Table 8, now v2 Table 10. The Figure 3 caption identifies prompt distributions as the uncertainty source but removes the previous heatmap standard-error bound. Existing simulation and repetition counts are unchanged; additional runs are not established.

E6.justification: Tables 8–9, 11–14, and 19 add substantial results on model distortions, kernels, temperature, prompt composition, and raw HumanEval accuracy. Temperature-mismatch power is 0.97–1.00. Table 11 reports Llama-3 8B int8 detection power of 0.30 at N=10m and 0.96 at N=50m, a newly reported budget comparison. The headline 77.4% power and 11-of-31 audit findings remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix C.1 adds the mathematical definition k(x,y)=exp(-Levenshtein(x,y)) for the new comparison kernel. The original hypotheses, MMD derivations, composite-null argument, and Appendix A proofs remain unchanged; swapping the order of the MMD arguments is equivalent notation.

C1.justification: The abstract qualifies undisclosed modifications from 'often' to 'possibly' and explicitly dates the commercial-API finding to Summer 2024. The main contributions, sample-efficiency claim, and 11-of-31 endpoint finding are retained.

C2.justification: New discussion explains heterogeneous detectability across models and prompt distributions, and how larger samples can offset character-space power losses. Appendix C.8 clarifies that distributional deviations can accompany either higher or lower accuracy and recommends manual quality review when MMD is large. These refine existing interpretations.

D1.justification: The new appendix experiments supply concrete specifications, including the exponential Levenshtein kernel and sample budgets and sequence lengths for additional comparisons. Appendix B's hardware, libraries, original data collection, and code/data access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds concurrent work by Sam, Finzi, and Kolter (2025), distinguishing it from this paper's false-positive-rate guarantees. The broader related-work framework and existing references are retained.

P1.justification: v2 tightens the introduction and related-work prose, adds explanatory discussion headings, and reorganizes Appendix C around the corresponding main-text experiments. The overall document structure remains stable, while the header changes from preprint to ICLR 2025 publication status.

P2.justification: The appendix gains substantial tabular presentation for model and kernel comparisons, temperature sensitivity, sample budgets, prompt composition, and raw accuracy. Existing power tables gain uncertainty entries, audit tables move, and several captions expand. The original figure graphics and qualitative sample boxes are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens validation through additional sensitivity tests, adds uncertainty to retained power results, and clarifies that distributional differences do not necessarily mean worse accuracy. These improve an already established empirical contribution without changing its central findings. Some new reporting remains incomplete, notably the unclear model identification in Tables 13–14, limiting the reproducibility gains.
